This test checks that hovering over a return statement reveals the result
type: one type per result, even when named results are grouped in a single
field (e.g. "a, b int" declares two results, not one).

-- a.go --
package a

func _() int {
    return 1 //@hover("return", "return 1", "returns (int)")
}

func _() (int, int) {
    return 1, 2 //@hover("return", "return 1, 2", "returns (int, int)")
}

// Grouped named results: each name is a separate result.
func _() (a, b int, c string) {
    return //@hover("return", "return", "returns (int, int, string)")
}

// Two grouped fields.
func _() (a, b int, c, d string) {
    return //@hover("return", "return", "returns (int, int, string, string)")
}

// Three names in one group.
func _() (a, b, c int) {
    return //@hover("return", "return", "returns (int, int, int)")
}

// Common idiom: one name per field.
func _() (n int, err error) {
    return //@hover("return", "return", "returns (int, error)")
}
